transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-05-09 15:00 PDT
- Duration: 57 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jenna (Voyanta), Ravi (Voyanta), Liam (Voyanta SRE), Sophie (Voyanta Security), Tom (Voyanta Product)

Summary:
Quick scoping to align on pilot success criteria, get traffic shape, confirm security constraints for a 4-week pilot where Redwood will replay Voyanta traffic on a dedicated pilot cluster and validate p95/p99 latency and cost per 1M tokens. Discussed QPS targets, concurrency envelope, and token-length distribution. Agreed next steps for data handoff and benchmark schedule.

Topics covered:
- Workload portraiting: QPS, spikes, concurrency, token distribution
- Bench harness and replay mechanics
- Success criteria and SLA gating for pilot
- Security: SOC2, SAML, KMS, VPC peering, audit logs
- Timeline: 4-week pilot with intermediate checkpoints

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): okay everyone thanks for joining, uh - I'm Maya, AE for Redwood Inference, with Carlos and Priya from our SE team. Jenna, do you want to kick us off with the use case context?
[00:20] Jenna (Voyanta): sure, thanks. we're building an outbound insight assistant for retail ops, so most calls are short prompts from agents looking up product status and rules. avg request is small but we do have a long tail for policy generation. we want to validate cost and latency at scale, and see if dedicated pilot capacity will meet our daytime peaks.
[00:45] Carlos (Redwood): cool — can you give ballpark QPS and the big spikes?
[00:50] Ravi (Voyanta): baseline qps is about 90 qps during peak hour across our EU and US regions, but we see short bursts up to ~800 qps for a couple minutes during promo triggers. most of those are smaller — think 40 to 150 input tokens and outputs around 60 to 180. but, uh, about 3-5% are long form, like 800-1200 output tokens for policy docs.
[01:20] Priya (Redwood): noted, the burst to 800 qps for minutes matters a lot for concurrency. are those bursts synchronous across regions or staggered?
[01:30] Liam (Voyanta): mostly synchronous — traffic orchestration triggers the fetch from all agents. so we've seen multi-region spikes coincide, that's part of why we've been worried about tail.
[01:45] Carlos: ok, so from a pilot standpoint we should model a topology with sustained baseline 90 qps and synthetic bursts up to 900 qps, with concurrency reflecting long context windows. do you have actual latency SLOs you're targeting?
[02:05] Jenna: internal target is p95 < 300ms for short prompts, p99 under 800ms. For those long policy generations, we care more about throughput and cost than p95.
[02:20] Maya: that's helpful. success criteria for the pilot we'd propose: 1) reproduce peak bursts with p95 within 1.2x of your internal target on pilot cluster, 2) show cost per 1M tokens within expected band, 3) validate fallback behavior if capacity constrained. Does that map to what you want?
[02:40] Tom (Voyanta): yes, and add security gating — we need to confirm no persistent logs of plaintext PII and KMS control of keys for private deployment.
[02:55] Sophie (Voyanta Security): correct, and we need SOC2 evidence and a runbook for audit logs. also SAML SSO into the console for RBAC.
[03:10] Carlos: we can provide our SOC2 report and an operations checklist. For pilot we can do either hosted dedicated fleet in our VPC-hosted tenant or a private deployment if you need on-prem. Which do you prefer to start with?
[03:30] Ravi: prefer hosted dedicated in our cloud account via VPC peering — faster to iterate. On-prem would be later if compliance demands.
[03:40] Priya: that maps well to a three-stage pilot: data capture & traffic export, replay + baseline benchmarks, and stress tests with bursts and model fallbacks. We typically run the replay in a sandboxed dedicated capacity so we can measure token-level cost.
[03:58] Jenna: timeline? we want results within 4 weeks.
[04:02] Maya: our standard plan: Week 0 (handoff) — Voyanta gives 3 days of anonymized logs + sample prompts; Week 1 — replay setup & smoke tests; Week 2 — baseline benchmark across your most-used models/variants; Week 3 — burst stress tests and regression checks; Week 4 — analysis, cost projection, and decision. So four weeks total.
[04:30] Ravi: sounds good. for the anonymized logs, what's the exact format you need?
[04:35] Carlos: CSV or parquet with columns: timestamp, request_id, model_hint, input_token_count, output_token_count, region, user_type. If you have KV cache patterns encoded, include session id. If not, we approximate.
[04:50] Liam: we can do parquet. we'll strip PII but keep session ids hashed.
[04:55] Sophie: for KMS, we need to know if Redwood supports customer-managed keys and HSM-backed keys.
[05:02] Carlos: yes, Redwood supports customer-managed keys and integrates with common KMS providers; HSM requirements we can scope as part of the private deployment discussion.
[05:12] Jenna: for the benchmark, we want to know exact scripts you'll run so we can validate results internally.
[05:17] Priya: we'll share a benchmark plan doc and the exact load scripts. Typically we run a mix of synthetic and replay-based load: 70% replay (to preserve real token mix) and 30% synthetic bursts to stress concurrency.
[05:33] Maya: let's talk numbers — you mentioned average input/output tokens, do you have distribution percentiles?
[05:38] Ravi: median input is 34 tokens, p90 120 tokens. output median 78, p90 240. long tail 99th around 950 tokens. About 12% of calls include multi-turn context with cached KV tokens adding ~150 tokens of prefix.
[06:00] Carlos: important note: multi-turn sessions increase KV cache pressure — that changes GPU mem footprint and can affect throughput. We'll include model variants with different kv-cache handling in the replay.
[06:15] Jenna: curious about routing and fallback — if the dedicated pilot runs out of capacity mid-burst, what happens?
[06:21] Maya: we support automatic fallback to a compatible, smaller quantized model variant, or re-route to a less expensive pool; we'll show failover latency and token-cost delta in the pilot. You can configure fallback policies.
[06:35] Tom: side question — are you able to instrument per-token latency traces? we need to map where tail latency arises.
[06:42] Priya: yes, the runtime exports token-level timing and per-request trace ids; we can push them to your tracing backend or give a downloadable CSV. Note: occasionally the transcription of our logs calls this 'per-token tic' — earlier reports show name variations, but the data is fine.
[07:00] Maya: on metrics we plan to collect: qps, concurrency, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory pressure, and cost per 1M input+output tokens. We'll also run quality checks against your eval prompts to surface regression risks when we switch quantized variants.
[07:25] Ravi: what's a realistic concurrency estimate from you for our numbers? if baseline qps 90 and average latency 200ms, that suggests concurrency ~18; but bursts to 800 qps with same latency would need concurrency ~160. Does that map to your sizing?
[07:40] Carlos: yes that's the right math. we'll dimension pilot cluster to handle 160 concurrent in the worst-case synthetic bursts with headroom. We'll also characterize GPU layouts (A100 vs H100 analogs) and show per-GPU QPS numbers for the model family you plan to use.
[08:00] Jenna: model family — we're prioritizing a 13B mixed-coder style model for latency/cost tradeoff. any thoughts?
[08:07] Priya: 13B is a common sweet spot. We'll recommend quantization profile and kernel selection; for example, 4-bit quant can cut mem by ~40% but may slightly degrade outputs for certain prompts. We'll include quality diffs in the report.
[08:30] Sophie: for compliance we'll need SAML metadata and user provisioning flow. how do we handle console access?
[08:36] Maya: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. We'll need an IdP metadata file and a small admin group mapping. We'll send an integration checklist.
[08:50] Tom: pricing — can you ballpark pilot cost for a 4-week dedicated sandbox?
[08:55] Maya: ballpark depends on hardware and model choices; for a dedicated pilot sized for your burst envelope, expect a monthly equivalent of mid-five figures — we'll put an exact SOW after we pick model variants. Pilot is typically free or discounted for committed evaluations; we'll include cost scenarios in the SOW.
[09:15] Jenna: can we run a mixed workload — i.e., retail assistants plus nightly batch policy gen without interfering with daytime latency?
[09:22] Carlos: yes we can schedule batch workloads during off-peak and isolate them to different queues. We'll show token-cost allocation per workload in the playbook.
[09:35] Sophie: audit log question — retention and export format?
[09:39] Maya: we support customizable retention up to 2 years for enterprise packs and export in JSON/CSV with trace ids; pilot will include 30-day retention by default.
[09:50] Unidentified (Legal): quick note — we need to review data processing addendum, can you send it?
[09:55] Maya: yes will attach DPA in the follow-up.
[10:02] Carlos: back to benchmarks — we'll propose two benchmark passes: (A) replay of real traffic for accuracy and cost, (B) stress/soak with synthetic bursts to exercise tail. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and token distribution.
[10:20] Ravi: when you say replay, do you preserve timing (real-time) or accelerate?
[10:24] Priya: both options. We usually run a timing-preserved replay for fidelity and a time-compressed stress replay for capacity testing. We'll label them clearly in the report.
[10:40] Jenna: are there any gotchas you usually see when customers bring hashed session IDs?
[10:45] Carlos: hashed IDs are fine; what's important is consistent hashing per session so we can approximate KV cache hits. If the hash is randomized between requests we lose cache signal.
[11:00] Tom: for the long outputs (policy docs), do you recommend chunking or streaming?
[11:05] Priya: streaming is best for user experience; chunking helps reduce peak memory but complicates reassembly. We'll test both.
[11:18] Maya: let's capture concrete success metrics to gate pilot success:
- Reproduce burst to 800-900 qps with p95 within 1.2x of target (target p95=300ms)
- Demonstrate fallback latency and cost delta <30% worse for fallback path
- Show cost per 1M tokens within +/- 20% of projected model/quantization run rates
- No security control gaps: SAML SSO working, KMS customer-managed keys confirmed, SOC2 docs provided

[12:05] Jenna: those are reasonable. if you can show a regression report that flags any quality delta >2% on our eval set we won't consider it acceptable.
[12:18] Priya: we'll run an automated eval and surface per-prompt diffs and a simple A/B score.

[12:30] Carlos: timeline recap — we'll:
- Day 0-3: Voyanta hands logs (parquet) + sample eval set
- Day 4-10: Redwood sets up replay and runs smoke + baseline
- Day 11-18: Baseline benchmarks and quantization experiments
- Day 19-25: Burst stress tests and failover scenarios
- Day 26-28: Final analysis and SOW for production recommendation

[13:05] Ravi: ok that maps to 4 weeks.
[13:08] Maya: any blockers on your side to start the handoff?
[13:12] Sophie: legal needs the DPA and a short scoping note for data residency — typically 48 hours to review.
[13:18] Unidentified (Legal): yes, 48-72 hours for initial review.
[13:22] Maya: we'll send DPA and SOW draft tomorrow.

(there is some cross talk and typing noises)

[13:45] Priya: a couple technical clarifications we'll include in the benchmark doc: exact model config (model id, quantization profile), concurrency shaping script, seed for synthetic generator, and metrics export schema.
[13:58] Carlos: also note that GPU kernel selection sometimes shows up in logs as 'kernal' or 'kernel sel' — a transcription artifact but the metric is kernel_version in the exported CSV.

[14:20] Jenna: any concerns about multi-region peering and latency for replay?
[14:25] Carlos: we'll replay regionally — deploy pilot nodes in both EU and US, measure intra-region latency; peering adds ~5-20ms typically, we'll document network margin.

[14:45] Tom: how will cost be reported? per-token with breakdown by model, quantization, and prefix cache hits?
[14:52] Maya: yes the report will show cost per 1M tokens and a breakdown by model variant and cache-hit vs miss. We'll also show projected monthly cost for production-scale QPS.

[15:10] Jenna: ok, last question — if we find quality regression after quantization, what are paths forward?
[15:15] Priya: options are 1) tune quantization profile, 2) use a slightly larger model for long-form, 3) hybrid routing (short prompts -> quantized fast model, long form -> full precision pool). We'll prototype routing in the pilot.

[15:35] Maya: good. let's recap next steps and owners — Carlos will prepare benchmark plan by 2027-05-12, Maya will send DPA, pricing deck, and pilot SOW by 2027-05-11, Ravi to share logs by 2027-05-14, Sophie to confirm security gating by 2027-05-13. We'll schedule the network/VPC checklist call for next Tuesday at 10am PT.
[15:55] Jenna: thanks all. excited to get started.

Recap and close:
- Pilot length: 4 weeks, handoff + replay + baseline + stress + analysis.
- Key metrics: qps/concurrency, p50/p95/p99, token distribution, GPU util, cost per 1M tokens, quality regression on eval set.
- Security: DPA, SOC2, SAML, KMS required.
- Next meetings: network checklist (Tue 10am PT), benchmark plan review (Carlos to present).
